claims.path: arm-scalable-vector-extension: identity, description, classification, event, date, place, earliest_record
claims.reason: Stephens, Hot Chips 28 title and slides 3–8 (https://community.arm.com/cfs-file/__key/telligent-evolution-components-attachments/01-3867-00-00-00-01-20-49/ARMv8_2D00_A-SVE-technology-Hot-Chips-v12.pdf) gives 22 August 2016, Cupertino, AArch64, variable lengths and predication. Stephens et al. 2017 introduction and §2 (https://alastairreid.github.io/papers/sve-ieee-micro-2017.pdf) explain 128–2048 bits in 128-bit steps and vector-length agnostic execution. This is a dated public presentation, not an invention date.

claims.path: fujitsu-a64fx: identity, description, grain, origin, organization, presentation and prototype events, earliest_record
claims.reason: Yoshida, Hot Chips 30 original slides 0–8 (https://old.hotchips.org/hc30/2conf/2.13_Fujitsu_HC30.Fujitsu.Yoshida.rev1.2.pdf) date disclosure 21 August 2018 and identify processor, post-K, 512-bit SVE, package memory and on-chip Tofu controller. Conference programme https://hc30.hotchips.org/index.html identifies venue and date; RIKEN https://www.riken.jp/en/news_pubs/news/2019/20191118_1/index.html reports 18 November 2019 and 768 processors in the Numazu prototype. This is an observed prototype, not the full installation.

Alappat et al., https://doi.org/10.1002/cpe.6512 §§2, 3.1 and Tables 1–2 report independently run A64FX FX1000 SVE instruction microbenchmarks, 512-bit width, standard ld1d reciprocal throughput 0.5 cycles; 2.2 GHz is the default. Date bounded by 30 July 2021 arXiv v2, not asserted test date.

Yoshida slides 1 and 5–8 explicitly identify SVE in the A64FX and collaboration; independently Alappat et al. §§2, 3.1, Tables 1–2 actually executed SVE instructions on A64FX. builds_on points from ISA to later implementation, not priority or exclusive development.

TOP500 https://www.top500.org/system/179807/ identifies A64FX and TofuD in the benchmarked system; Yoshida slides 1, 6 and 8 and RIKEN https://www.r-ccs.riken.jp/en/fugaku/about/ describe component and system. Independent Diehl et al. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2304.11002 §§VI.D and VIII ran an SVE-enabled stellar simulation on up to 1024 Fugaku A64FX nodes. requires is scoped to the documented 2020 configuration.

claims.path: riken-fujitsu-fugaku links from fujitsu-tofu-interconnect-2, candidate finding and evidence
claims.reason: Fujitsu FX1000 white paper p.7 https://treasures.scss.tcd.ie/miscellany/TCD-SCSS-X.20121208.002/Fujitsu-primehpc-fx1000-hard-en.pdf explicitly bases TofuD on Tofu2 and says 6D topology originated for K and continues in both. Watanabe et al. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11227-024-06201-x §§4–5 measured software on TofuD, not design transfer from Tofu2. Dongarra repeats designer account. Keep inherited design elements candidate pending independent informative evidence; no relationship was promoted.

Independently checked original Stephens and Yoshida presentations; 2019 RIKEN prototype report; conference programme; RIKEN operator description; TOP500 system record; Alappat instruction measurements; Diehl application tests; Watanabe communication experiments; Fujitsu TofuD white paper. Source notes and lane findings reflect their different scope and do not treat tests as proof of Tofu2 inheritance. Search of baseline records found existing Fugaku/Tofu2, no separate A64FX or SVE record.

claims.path: armv8-a-64-bit-architecture: identity, description, domain, grain, preview and publication events, dates, earliest_record
claims.reason: Arm Architecture Group, ARMv8 Instruction Set Overview issue 15.0 (https://www.cs.princeton.edu/courses/archive/fall22/cos217/reading/ArmInstructionSetOverview.pdf), cover, §1.1.2, §§2–3, is dated 11 November 2011, identifies first non-confidential issue and details AArch64, A64 fixed-width 32-bit instruction encodings and 64-bit registers. Arm’s David Brash (https://developer.arm.com/community/arm-community-blogs/b/architectures-and-processors-blog/posts/the-armv8-a-architecture-and-its-ongoing-development) opening dates the initial public preview to October 2011. Neither date implies first silicon.

Stephens 2016 https://developer.arm.com/community/arm-community-blogs/b/servers-and-cloud-computing-blog/posts/technology-update-the-scalable-vector-extension-sve-for-the-armv8-a-architecture explicitly targets AArch64 execution and allocates SVE in A64 encoding space. His Hot Chips deck p.3 explicitly distinguishes SVE from Advanced SIMD. Alappat et al. https://doi.org/10.1002/cpe.6512 §§2, 3.1, Tables 1–2 independently execute SVE instruction microbenchmarks on Armv8.2-A A64FX, corroborating deployed combination rather than independently proving 2011 design history. The relation is correctly directed from SVE to its substrate.

claims.path: follow-on source records and lane report additions
claims.reason: Independently read the 2011 overview, Brash 2014 opening, Stephens 2016 encoding account, and Alappat methods and instruction measurements. The lane confines architecture history to a dated preview and non-confidential specification, and does not claim transfer from Advanced SIMD or working silicon in 2011.
